title: test(cli): make the app-anchored serve e2e prove a BOOT, not just a resolution
body:
Fixes #12567

## Ruling 1 first: the measurement, and what it decided

The card offered three shapes and ruled that the choice belongs to a measurement rather than to cost. The question: **does anything in the repo already prove `os serve` boots with an app-local cluster driver?** If something did, this file should have been renamed to say `resolves`. If nothing did, the boot coverage had to be built here.

Swept on `527e0505d`, across the 2823 test files this workspace tracks:

| query | population | hits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sets `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` on a spawned child | test files | **1** — this file. `serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts` names the variable in prose and spawns nothing |
| `registerClusterDriver` | test files | **0** |
| `cluster`, any spelling | `packages/qa/**` (190 files: dogfood + every conformance suite) | **0** |

Reverse-checks for both zeros, against terms known present in the same population and never a substring of the term under test:

- test files — `checkMultiNodeAllowed` → 5 files, `defineCluster` → 2, `service-cluster` → 7.
- `packages/qa/**` — `dogfood` → 86 files, `serve` → 74.

And the zero is structural rather than incidental: `serve.ts`'s entire cluster block sits behind `if (__clusterDriver && __clusterDriver !== 'memory')`, so a test that never sets the variable never loads a cluster package at all. No other banner-reaching e2e file in `packages/cli/test` could have been covering this.

⇒ **Nothing proved it. Route A.**

## What changed, plainly: this file measures MORE than it did

⚠️ A decision being recorded, not a repair being described.

Before, `FAKE_DRIVER` was one `console.error` that registered nothing, so `serve` walked on to `Cluster driver "redis" is not registered` and the child exited 1 without ever calling `listen()`. The file proved `serve` **RESOLVES** an app-local cluster driver; it never proved `serve` **BOOTS** with one — while its test names and its `Press Ctrl+C to stop` settle alternative both read as though a boot were in scope.

The fixture driver now registers a driver, and both happy-path children boot through to a ready banner. Reproduced standalone before the file was touched, replicating the fixture verbatim:

```
registering = false   settled via exit    at  9.6s   markers ok/ok   "is not registered" true    banner false
registering = true    settled via waitFor at 12.4s   markers ok/ok   "is not registered" false   banner true
                                                     API: http://localhost:42783/  (= the port asked for)
```

The handover the fixture needs is stated in the file's anti-vacuity note: the driver registry is module-scope state in the framework's own `@objectstack/service-cluster`, so the fixture is handed that module's ESM entry. Registering into the app's fixture *copy* would write to a Map nothing reads — and registering into the CJS twin would do the same, silently, which is why the entry is taken from the package's own `exports["."].import` rather than from `createRequire().resolve()`. `frameworkClusterEsmEntry()` resolves by specifier from `@objectstack/runtime` (the module whose registry decides this boot) and verifies the manifest it lands on by `name`. **No new spawn**, so nothing new is owed to `check:cli-test-child-env` — the gate that stopped the previous attempt, and it is green.

## Ruling 2: the closed loop, closed

`SETTLED` no longer matches either marker. Both markers are printed **mid-boot**, so waking on one handed the assertions a process that had not finished — and, before the driver registered, one that was about to die. The rule the file now states and keeps is mechanical:

> `SETTLED` may match only TERMINAL outcomes, never mid-boot progress.

It is now `/Press Ctrl\+C to stop|does not declare it/` — the two outcomes the cases discriminate between, each asserted by one case and turning another case RED.

The boot itself is asserted **without** re-reading the text that woke the run: `expect(run.both).not.toContain('is not registered')` and `expect(run.outcome).toBe('matched')`, where `outcome` (`matched` / `exited` / `timeout`) is a fact about the harness rather than a string in the child's buffer. `timeout` is the case no string assertion can reach: a child that printed both markers and then hung short of `listen()` satisfies every one of them.

## ⚠️ One claim of the card's that did NOT survive re-measurement

The card read the old happy path as a closed loop that **"cannot fail"**, on the ground that `toContain(DRIVER_MARK)` was also one of `SETTLED`'s alternatives. That inference is **false on this tree**, and the file now carries the correction so it is not re-derived.

`finish()` has FOUR call sites and only ONE is gated on `waitFor` — the others are the child's `exit`, its `error` and the timeout. So a run reaches the assertions whether or not `waitFor` ever matched. A `serve` that re-anchored at the CWD prints `does not declare it` for the DECLARED app, settles on THAT alternative, and the marker assertions go red. Measured by replaying the harness's settle structure verbatim against three children:

```
child prints DRIVER_MARK, stays up            settled via waitFor   assertion GREEN
child prints nothing matching, exits 1        settled via exit      assertion RED
child prints "does not declare it", exits 1   settled via waitFor   assertion RED
```

What WAS true is the narrower thing this PR fixes, and it is the load-bearing half of the card: the markers are **mid-boot**, so the wake told the assertions nothing about the outcome. The card's second half — resolves is not boots, and the port apparatus inert as a consequence — is confirmed exactly as filed.

## Ruling 3: the port apparatus, updated rather than deleted

Both calls stay. The header note that explains them is **updated**, because the tree it was written for is no longer this one:

- **`portDriftError()` — now LIVE** on the two happy-path runs. They print a complete banner, so `boundPortFromBanner()` answers `bound` and the port the harness asked for is really compared against the one the child bound. Still `null` on the undeclared leg, which dies before `listen()` — that helper's own stated contract, not a gap.
- **`portContentionError()` — still insurance**, and not for the reason the old note gave. Its silence never depended on the banner: these children spawn through `bin/run-dev.js`, which pins `NODE_ENV=development` before argv is parsed, so `serve`'s auto-shift branch is open and a taken port is a hop to the next free one, never the bind failure that helper reads for. That is a property of the **spawn posture**, so booting to a banner cannot make it fire.

The old paragraph's "do not make the read-back live by gating resolution on the banner" is retired with its reason stated: it said "no child here prints one", and now they do.

## Verification — all at `874c2012e`, the final commit

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 \
  test/serve-app-anchored-optional-import.e2e.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Duration  33.48s
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 35s
```

Gate union, 21 families, all `EXIT=0` — exit codes captured **before** any pipe (`cmd > log 2>&1; code=$?`), and each family's verdict read from the line the gate itself printed:

`check:cli-test-child-env` · `check:nul-bytes` · `check:engine-double-contract` · `check:where-matcher` · `check:query-options-erasure` · `check:objectql-double-limit` · `check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `check:test-source-alias` · `check:type-check-coverage` · `check:type-source-resolution` · `check:published-files` · `check:slot-lookup` · `check:page-declaration-shape` · `check-ci-filter-parity` · `check-comment-mask-adoption` · `check-cross-package-test-inputs` · `check-plugin-teardown-shape` · `check:i18n` · `check:i18n-coverage` · `check:type-check-debt` · plus the `lint.yml` workspace build (70/70) those last three needed.

The ratchet this diff could actually move:

```
check-type-check-coverage --re-measure: OK — 31 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 328.5s,
1687 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number.
```

That one matters here specifically: `@objectstack/cli`'s TEST_DEBT entry records 146 and says *"RECORDED EXACTLY, no bootstrap margin: this layer has never been gated, so the first new error in it should go red rather than be absorbed."* It did not move.

⚠️ **NOT MEASURED, stated rather than implied.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` exits 0, but its program is `include: ["src"]` — `tsc --listFiles` finds this file **0** times, so that green says nothing about it. What does cover it is the ledger run above, plus an ad-hoc program over this file and `test/helpers/serve-process.ts` with `rootDir` neutralised: **0 errors**.

**Narrowing declared:** the full `packages/cli` suite does not finish in this container's foreground window, so only the edited file was run locally. CI runs the farm.

## Scope

`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` and `serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts` are untouched (both held this round). One file changed, +277/−50. No changeset: test-only, publishes nothing — hence `skip-changeset`.
